plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large, daisy-like flower head made up of golden ray florets surrounding a dark central disk. The flower heads track the sun when young. It is widely grown as an ornamental, a seed crop and an oilseed crop.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated across Europe, Russia, Ukraine, the United States and temperate Asia
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds follow the sun from east to west in a process called heliotropism, but mature blooms stop moving and generally face east.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of small tubular flowers. It thrives in full sun and well-drained soil, and the blooms attract bees and butterflies in large numbers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer, with peak bloom in July and August in many regions
plants.location: Native to the western Mediterranean; widely cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, Tasmania and the Pacific Northwest of the United States
plants.funFact: The name lavender is thought to come from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans used it to scent baths and laundry.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large round leaves that rise above the water and showy, many-petaled flowers on tall stalks. The leaves have a waxy surface that makes water bead up and roll off. It grows in shallow ponds, lakes and wetlands.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, peaking from July to August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Asia, from India and China to Japan and northern Australia; cultivated in water gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus seeds can remain viable for centuries, and one seed about 1,300 years old was successfully germinated.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A shrub with the largest flower head of any protea. The bloom is a bowl of pink-tipped bracts surrounding a central cluster of tiny flowers, and it is set among leathery, oval leaves. It is adapted to fire-prone, nutrient-poor fynbos soils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering often beginning in August
plants.location: Southwestern and southern coastal South Africa, in fynbos vegetation; cultivated in Australia, Hawaii and California
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and its genus is named after Proteus, the Greek sea god who could change shape.
